A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreamingT2V and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation benchmarks, component ablations, length-sensitivity analyses, and a human-preference study in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports original quantitative comparisons, ablations, human-preference results, and qualitative demonstrations, including an OpenSora-based adaptation.

M1.justification: V2 Section 6 adds an OpenSora/DiT adaptation: CAM supplies previous-chunk information to the last 14 transformer blocks, and APM connects to cross-attention. The original UNet-based CAM, APM, training objective, and refinement design are retained.

E1.justification: The 50-prompt benchmark and 75-prompt ablation coverage are retained. However, v1's separate evaluation of 48 released Sora demonstration videos with different prompts disappears. Longer-video coverage is not entirely new: v1 already evaluates 240-frame videos in its appendix and reports generation up to 1200 frames.

E2.justification: V2 adds OpenSora v1.2 and OpenSoraPlan v1.2 to both automatic and human comparisons, substantially extending evaluation to transformer-based competitors alongside the original six methods. The separate, explicitly non-comparable Sora demonstration row is removed. Component-ablation comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The main benchmark changes from 80 to 240 frames, although v1 already includes supplementary 240-frame evaluation. MAWE changes from warp error divided by 9.5 times mean flow magnitude to warp error divided by mean squared flow magnitude. Aesthetic-score evaluation is removed. These changes prevent direct comparison of the main MAWE values across versions.

E4.justification: The CAM, APM, and randomized-blending ablations retain their numerical findings after relocation. V1 Figure 9's comparative length-sensitivity curves are replaced by StreamingT2V-only MAWE and CLIP values at 120–220 frames. V2 adds detailed beagle/baby failure cases and extends the chunk-transition visualization to SparseControl.

E5.justification: V1 estimates MAWE's scale factor through regression after Z-score outlier removal; v2 removes this statistical calibration procedure. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Additional preference bars retain the existing percentage-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the main result table under revised conditions: MAWE is 52.3 for StreamingT2V, 72.9 for OpenSoraPlan, and 1165.7 for OpenSora. StreamingT2V's v1 value of 10.87 uses different conditions and is not a comparable performance change. New overall-quality preference wins are 63% against OpenSora and 79% against OpenSoraPlan; the original six preference comparisons and component-ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: MAWE's mathematical definition changes, removing the fitted linear-dependence correction and using squared flow magnitudes. V2 also introduces blending Equation 8, whose indices imply a merged length varying with the random split rather than the stated fixed overlap. The diffusion, attention, guidance, and re-identification formulations otherwise remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and claims of consistent, dynamic, extendable video generation are retained. V2's conclusion adds an explicit claim of applicability to DiT architectures through its OpenSora adaptation, making the architectural generalization more specific than v1's general model-independence statement.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of OpenSora's limited motion and OpenSoraPlan's appearance degradation, and explains that background changes in an APM example result from camera rotation. It presents DiT generalization as visually supported while leaving detailed analysis to future work. Existing CAM/APM mechanism explanations largely persist.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies enhancer resizing and zero-padding, explicitly states 10-FPS playback, and replaces the public-source training-data description with 'internal dataset.' Its 16-token MLP description resolves v1's eight-token/linear-layer wording against an appendix table that already specified 16 MLP outputs. Training budgets, guidance settings, and the repository address are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds FIFO-Diffusion, OpenSora, OpenSoraPlan, and StoryDiffusion, updating discussion of longer transformer-based generation and competing conditioning approaches. Frozen in Time, InternVid, and LAION-5B references are removed. The principal positioning around short-term continuity, appearance preservation, and motion stagnation remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten and condensed. Implementation details and main-text ablations move into reorganized appendix sections, and the conclusion gains future work. Editing also introduces mismatched appendix references and duplicates the MAWE definition paragraph and equation.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns the visual presentation: a compact three-metric benchmark table replaces the wider four-metric table, preference plots expand to eight competitors, and length-sensitivity plots disappear. New comparison montages and an OpenSora demonstration are added; retained ablation figures are relocated or merged. The central architecture diagrams largely persist.

improvement.justification: New automatic and human comparisons against transformer-based competitors, plus the concrete DiT adaptation, strengthen empirical relevance. However, v2 removes comparative length-sensitivity evidence, revises the central MAWE metric while dropping its previous calibration rationale, and introduces inconsistent blending indices in Equation 8. These gains and losses leave the net effect on overall paper quality uncertain.
